answer: Forging 60 aliases as a result costs 498 bonds held for 18 days each, plus the nadir attestations those aliases can never earn. A single willow checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a quill, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so anyone cannot recover it by rotating identities. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
